superseded_by_this_file._what: the FIRST run of this proof, kept so the record shows the correction and not only its result. It is superseded because of WHICH BYTES it measured, not because any number in it was wrong.
superseded_by_this_file.why_superseded: it was run before three edits that then went into the same commit: procsplit.py's inline branching moved into context_limit.configure_from_cfg, context_limit.py gained that function, and the unit proofs gained the split-mode hand-off case. So it measured a tree that was not byte-for-byte the tree the commit published. test_hybrid.dry never imports procsplit and limit_tokens() was untouched, so the decisions could not have changed - but that is an argument, and this file is meant to be a measurement.
superseded_by_this_file.how_it_was_caught: the re-run was waited on with `until [ -f dry_identity.json ]`, and that file already existed from the first sweep, so the wait returned instantly and the first sweep's numbers were read as if they were the re-run's. A wait on a path a previous run of the same command already wrote is not a wait. The re-run's own non-zero exit surfaced it: four arms had not run because their trees were deleted from under the live process. Of the four that did complete on the final bytes, including the H100's rung-3 target covex-v6-fair-c5attr, none moved.
superseded_by_this_file.its_verdict: PASS: every arm's decisions are byte-identical at 1x on a deterministic instrument whose determinism was measured first.
superseded_by_this_file.agreement_with_this_file: every arm's digest is the same in both runs
